info.title: RunStack Automation API Gdba Sql
info.summary: RunStack Infrastructure Automation API — Gdba Sql scope
info.description:
API for triggering AWS SSM RunCommand, SSM Automation, and EC2 Actions via RunStack.

## Authentication
This API supports two authentication flows:
- **User auth (QuickSuite)**: OAuth2 Authorization Code flow via Azure AD SSO.
- **System auth (Dynatrace/EventBridge)**: OAuth2 Client Credentials flow.

Both flows use Cognito user pool (us-east-1_ViOMjHyze) and require the `runstack-api/notify` scope.

## Authorization
User tokens are granted `authorized=true` through either of two independent paths:
- **Platform-wide access** — user is in the `runstack-admins` or `runstack-operators` Cognito group. These users can see and act on every instance across every app, with no scoping applied.
- **App-scoped access** — user has at least one entry in the `runstack-app-access` table mapping their email to one or more `app_id` values. These users are restricted to only the instances belonging to their assigned app(s), enforced on both `GET /app-instances` and `POST /notify`.

Machine tokens (Dynatrace/EventBridge) are always allowed and are never subject to app-level scoping.

Users with neither group membership nor an app-access entry receive `403 Forbidden` on every endpoint.

## Recommended Discovery + Polling Flow
1. `GET /app-instances` — discover which instances the current user is allowed to act on
2. `POST /notify` — trigger automation on one of those instances, get back `job_id`
3. Poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` every 3-5 seconds until `status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`
4. Read `ec2_state` from the response for EC2-Action jobs

## EC2 Action Flow
1. `POST /notify` with `automation_type: EC2-Action` and `automation_data: {}`
2. Step Function calls `ec2:DescribeInstances` via cross-account role
3. Poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` — when `status=COMPLETED`, read `ec2_state` field

## EC2 Start/Stop Flow
1. `POST /notify` with `automation_type: SSM-Automation`
2. Set `DocumentName` to `AWS-StartEC2Instance` or `AWS-StopEC2Instance`
3. Poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}` until `status=COMPLETED`

## Synchronous Status Check Flow (NEW)
For status-check-only calls (EC2-Action or a short-running SSM-RunCommand), use `POST /notify-sync` instead of `POST /notify` — it triggers the automation, polls internally for up to ~25 seconds, and returns the final job result directly, with no client-side polling required. If the job hasn't completed within that window, it returns `202` with the `job_id` so the caller can fall back to manually polling `GET /jobs/{jobId}`. Do NOT use `/notify-sync` for Start/Stop actions that may run longer than ~25 seconds — use `POST /notify` + `GET /jobs/{jobId}` polling for those instead.

## v3.0.0 — full API surface
Extended from the v2.9.0 notify/notify-sync-focused spec to cover every route currently deployed: admin (users, team capabilities, Cognito group audit — all admin-role-gated), SSM document catalog, EventBridge schedules, jobs DLQ, Tidal agent mapping, batch/async healthchecks, Dynatrace AG discovery, DR failover (GDBA team-capability-gated), auth callback/local login, and S3 uploads. Role-based and team-capability-based restrictions are enforced server-side (require_role() / require_gdba_capability()) and are documented in each operation's description, not expressed as separate OAuth2 scopes — every user-facing operation uses the same `runstack-api/notify` scope shown in `security`.

get.summary: List instances the current user is allowed to access
get.description:
Returns the EC2 instances scoped to the authenticated user.

- **Platform admins/operators** receive every instance in the catalog, with `apps` set to `["ALL"]`.
- **App-scoped users** receive only instances belonging to the app(s) listed in their `runstack-app-access` entry.
- Optionally filter the result down to a single app using the `app_id` query parameter — this is rejected with `403` if the requesting user is not scoped to that app.

Use this endpoint before `POST /notify` to know which `resource_id` values are valid for the current user, rather than guessing or hardcoding instance IDs.

parameters.name: app_id
parameters.description: Restrict the result to a single app the user is scoped to

200.description: Instances the user is allowed to access

403.description: Forbidden — user has no app access entries, or requested app_id is not in the user's scope

post.summary: Trigger a status check and wait synchronously for the result (status checks only — do not use for Start/Stop)
post.description:
Same request body as `POST /notify`. Internally triggers the automation and polls `GET /jobs/{jobId}` on the server side for up to ~25 seconds, returning the final job result directly — no client-side polling loop required.

Use this for: EC2-Action status checks, and short-running SSM-RunCommand status scripts (e.g. the SAP DB/ASCS/PAS/AAS status checks, which typically complete in a few seconds).

Do NOT use this for Start/Stop actions — those can legitimately run longer than the ~25 second window this endpoint waits before giving up, and API Gateway's own 29-second integration timeout makes waiting longer than that impossible for a synchronous call. Use `POST /notify` + `GET /jobs/{jobId}` polling for Start/Stop instead.

If the job has not completed within ~25 seconds, this returns `202` with the `job_id` — fall back to polling `GET /jobs/{jobId}` manually in that case.

EC2-Status-Check-Sync.summary: Get EC2 instance state, waiting for the result

SSM-RunCommand-Status-Sync.summary: Run a short status-check script, waiting for the result

200.description: Job completed within the wait window — final result included

202.description: Still running after ~25s — fall back to polling GET /jobs/{jobId} using the returned job_id

example.message: Still running after 25s — poll GET /jobs/{jobId} to continue.

403.description: Forbidden — either the user has no authorization path (not in an allowed group and no app-access entry), or the targeted instance does not belong to one of the user's assigned apps

get.description:
Returns the most recent automation execution matching the provided filters. For EC2-Action jobs, the response includes `ec2_state` field with the instance state.

**Note**: Prefer `GET /jobs/{jobId}` when you have a specific job ID from `POST /notify`.

parameters.name: resource_id
parameters.description: EC2 instance ID — filter by specific instance

get.description: Returns the latest automation execution history with pagination support.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of recent jobs to return

parameters.name: last_key
parameters.description: Pagination token from previous response next_token field

get.summary: Get automation execution status by job ID
get.description:
**Primary polling endpoint.** Use the `job_id` returned from `POST /notify` to poll this endpoint.

- Poll every 3-5 seconds until `status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`
- For EC2-Action jobs, read `ec2_state` when `status=COMPLETED`
- `ec2_state` values: `running`, `stopped`, `pending`, `stopping`, `terminated`

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Automation job identifier returned by POST /notify

post.summary: Check EC2 power state for a given instance

resource_id.description: EC2 instance ID for the host to check

get.description: Same underlying instance catalog as GET /app-instances, with an additional optional `server_name` filter for exact-match lookup by hostname.

parameters.name: server_name
parameters.description: Exact-match filter by server_name or name

404.description: server_name filter provided but no match found

post.summary: Trigger SQL DB health checks for a batch of servers from a SharePoint-managed list
post.description: Requires the "sql-db-healthcheck" team capability. If server_name is provided, dispatches a single health-check job for that one server (skips the SharePoint fetch). If omitted, reads the full server list from SharePoint (folder/file overridable), resolves each to a catalog instance, and dispatches one health-check job per server. Same response shape (total_servers/jobs) either way.

server_name.description: Optional. If given, runs a single-server health check for this server only, instead of the full SharePoint sweep. Resolved the same way as GET /app-instances?server_name=.

sharepoint_folder.description: Optional. Only used for the bulk sweep (ignored if server_name is given).

sharepoint_file.description: Optional. Only used for the bulk sweep (ignored if server_name is given).

post.summary: Trigger an async pre-check (e.g. disk usage) on an instance
post.description: Dispatches an SSM command and returns immediately with a check_id — poll GET /assess/{checkId} for the result.

get.summary: Poll the result of an async pre-check
get.description: Poll until status is COMPLETE or FAILED.

get.summary: List all known SQL Availability Groups from Dynatrace
get.description: Returns AG names discoverable via Dynatrace host groups.

get.summary: List servers belonging to one AG
Trigger an async SQL AG role check (PRIMARY/SECONDARY per replica)
get.description: Async — returns 202 with a job_id immediately. Poll GET /dynatrace/ags/{AGName}/roles/{JobId} for the result. This is the required first step before POST /dr-failover/{AGName}/plan.

get.summary: Poll the result of an AG role check
get.description: Poll until roles are returned (non-empty result with PRIMARY identified).

get.summary: Get DR failover thresholds/configuration for a SQL AG

post.summary: Validate preconditions and issue a confirmation token for a SQL AlwaysOn AG DR failover
post.description: Requires the "sql-dr-failover" team capability, scoped to this AG. Requires a completed role_check_job_id from GET /dynatrace/ags/{AGName}/roles/{JobId} first. Evaluates preconditions (log queue size, transaction age); if all pass, creates a run record, issues a short-lived confirmation_token, and posts a Teams approval card.

target_replica.description: Required only if both an HA and DR target are available (needs_target_choice)

200.description: Plan result — all_pass true means a confirmation_token was issued

400.description: Missing role_check_job_id, role check not yet complete, ambiguous target (needs_target_choice), or preconditions failed

post.summary: Execute a previously-planned SQL AlwaysOn AG DR failover
post.description: Requires the "sql-dr-failover" team capability, scoped to this AG, plus a valid unexpired confirmation_token from POST .../plan and confirm="YES" as an explicit double-confirmation.

post.summary: Approve or reject a pending SQL AG DR failover from the Microsoft Teams approval card
post.description: Called by the Teams approval card's button action, not typically called directly by API clients — authenticated by a shared secret rather than a user token.

get.summary: Get the status of a SQL AG DR failover run
get.description: Poll until status is a terminal state (COMPLETED, EXECUTE_FAILED, REJECTED, etc).

cognitoClientCredentials.description: Cognito OAuth2 Client Credentials Flow — for system-to-system integrations (Dynatrace, EventBridge, schedulers). No user login required. Never subject to app-level instance scoping.

cognitoUserAuth.description:
Cognito OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow — for user-initiated flows via Amazon QuickSuite. Users authenticate with corporate Azure AD credentials via SAML SSO.

A successfully authenticated user is granted `runstack:authorized=true` through either:
- Membership in the `runstack-admins` or `runstack-operators` Cognito group (platform-wide access, no instance scoping), or
- An entry in the `runstack-app-access` table mapping their email to one or more app IDs (scoped access — restricted to instances belonging to their assigned app(s))

Users with neither receive `runstack:authorized=false` and are blocked with `403` on every endpoint.

scopes.openid: OpenID Connect — required for user identity

id.description: Unique request identifier — used for correlation

account_id.description: AWS account ID from instance catalog

resource_id.description: EC2 instance ID. For app-scoped users, must be an instance returned by GET /app-instances

automation_type.description: SSM-Automation: run SSM automation document. SSM-RunCommand: run command on instances. EC2-Action: get EC2 instance state via Step Function cross-account role.

AutomationData.description: Automation parameters. For EC2-Action, pass empty object `{}`. For SSM types, DocumentName is required.

DocumentName.description: AWS SSM document name. Required for SSM-Automation and SSM-RunCommand. Not required for EC2-Action.

InstanceIds.description: Used for SSM-RunCommand. Should contain the resource_id.

Parameters.description: SSM document parameters. Values must be arrays of strings.

ec2_state.description: EC2 instance state — populated for EC2-Action jobs when status=COMPLETED

exit_code.description: The script's own process exit code (distinct from SSM-level status). -1 or absent means SSM did not report an exit code (e.g. EC2-Action jobs).

script_result.description: PASSED if exit_code == 0, FAILED if exit_code is non-zero. Note: a status script using "; true" always exits 0, so script_result will always read PASSED for those calls -- read the parsed output field instead for actual service health.

output.description: Raw stdout captured from the RunCommand script (e.g. the JSON printed by check_oracle_status.sh, or plain text from other scripts). This is the field to parse for actual service state -- status and script_result only describe whether the command executed, not what it found.

next_token.description: Pagination token — pass as last_key query param to get next page

instances.description: Instances the current user is scoped to

apps.description: App IDs this response was scoped to. Contains ["ALL"] for admins/operators.
